title: Rabbi Chinena son of Rabbi Assi
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.
copyright: English translation and editorial notes © 2026 Joshua Waxman. All rights reserved.
paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 1:1, folio 3a, relates: Chinena son of Rabbi Assi was maysan (a quarrelsome man or a physician); he threw a bill of divorce to his wife, and she began to cry out; her neighbors came up, he snatched it from her and gave her blank paper. The case came before the Rabbis, and they were concerned (Hyman suggests perhaps because he was a Kohen, and even the scent of a bill of divorce disqualifies her for him). In Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 3:8: Chinena son of Rav Assi bar Mamal in the name of Rabbi Lazar. In Jerusalem Talmud Terumot 4:3: “Rabbi Chanina bar Issi said: Bar Kappara taught only,” etc. In Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 7:2, folio 29a: Rabbi Chanina bar Yasa in the name of Rav Yehudah; Hyman proposes there Rabbi Chanina bar Yakah in the name of Rabbi Yehudah, as in Jerusalem Talmud Beitzah, chapter 1, end of halakhah 10. In Jerusalem Talmud Maaserot 1:7: “Chananyah son of Rabbi Yasa said: How do Rabbi Yehudah and the Rabbis disagree?” In Bereshit Rabbah 4:4: “Rabbi Chanina bar Assi said: At times the world and its fullness cannot contain the glory of His divinity.”

notes.text: פלגאה means contentious or quarrelsome, without the invented ritual qualifier; physician is Hyman’s alternative explanation of מיסן. His possible priesthood and disqualifying scent-of-divorce explanation remains conjectural, and Assi/Issi/Yasa/Yakah forms are kept.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 1:1 directly contains the bill-of-divorce, outcry, neighbors and blank-paper episode. Maysan’s lexical alternatives, the possible priesthood explanation and the Assi/Issi/Yasa/Yakah corrections remain Hyman’s account; these name forms are not merged.
